content: Rifampin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of erdafitinib by altering its metabolism. It is recommended to avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Erdafitinib, in turn, increases the levels or effects of rifampin via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If coadministration is unavoidable, separate the administration of erdafitinib and P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index by at least 6 hours. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ergotamine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of erlotinib by both P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity and CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of escitalopram by inducing both CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of estradiol (oral and vaginal forms) and conjugated or esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of eszopiclone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Note that rifampin decreases zopiclone AUC by 80%, and a similar effect is expected with eszopiclone. Ethanol reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is more likely with chronic ethanol use. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use a nonhormonal contraceptive method as an alternative. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ethosuximide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ethotoin by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of etoposide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of etrasimod by inducing CYP3A4, CYP2C8, and CYP2C9 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels of etravirine by inducing CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of eucalyptus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of everolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Coadministration is contraindicated. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of exemestane by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. For patients receiving exemestane with a potent CYP3A4 inducer, the recommended dose is 50 mg daily after a meal. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of felbamate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of felodipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of fenfluramine by an unspecified mechanism. Coadministration with drugs that increase serotonin may increase the risk of serotonin syndrome. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, transmucosal) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may lead to reduced fentanyl plasma concentrations, lack of efficacy, or withdrawal syndrome in dependent patients. After stopping a CYP3A4 inducer, fentanyl plasma concentrations may increase, potentially prolonging therapeutic and adverse effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of fesoterodine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of fexofenadine by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of finasteride by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of finerenone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of flibanserin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly decrease flibanserin systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases the levels of fluconazole by increasing its metabolism. Fluconazole reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of flurazepam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of flurbiprofen by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin increases the toxicity of fluvastatin by an unspecified mechanism. It also decreases fluvastatin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases the levels of fosamprenavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels of fosinopril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of fosphenytoin by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Fostamatinib increases the levels or effects of rifampin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Concomitant use may increase concentrations of P-gp substrates. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of fostemsavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated, as it significantly reduces temsavir (active moiety) plasma concentrations, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of frovatriptan by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of fruquintinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of futibatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
